questions.prompt: What is an enumeration in Swift?

options.text: A custom type that defines a fixed group of related choices safely.
options.explanation: Right. Swift enums define a fixed set of related choices with strong type safety.

options.text: A class that automatically inherits stored properties from a parent class.
options.explanation: Enums are value types and cannot inherit from classes.

options.text: A collection that stores unordered key-value pairs like a dictionary.
options.explanation: Dictionaries store key-value pairs; enums define distinct named cases.

options.text: A mutable list of values indexed by sequential integer positions.
options.explanation: Arrays store ordered values by integer index; enums define fixed choices.

questions.prompt: How do Swift enums differ from enums in C or Objective-C by default?

options.text: Swift enum cases start at 1 instead of 0 by default.
options.explanation: Swift enum cases do not receive default integer values at all.

options.text: Swift enum cases do not get integer values by default unless you declare a raw type.
options.explanation: Right. Unlike C, Swift enum cases are distinct values without default numbers.

options.text: Swift enums are reference types shared across variables on the heap.
options.explanation: Swift enums are value types, not reference types.

options.text: Swift enums must always declare an explicit raw type like Int or String.
options.explanation: Raw types are optional in Swift enums.

questions.prompt: Are Swift enumerations value types or reference types?

options.text: They are reference types shared across all scopes in the app.
options.explanation: Swift enums are value types, not reference types.

options.text: They are reference types when they have associated values, and value types otherwise.
options.explanation: Enums are always value types, even with associated values.

options.text: They are value types, meaning they are copied when assigned or passed to functions.
options.explanation: Right. Enums are value types and are copied on assignment.

options.text: They become reference types when you store them inside an array or dictionary.

questions.prompt: Why must a switch statement over a Swift enum be exhaustive?

options.text: So the compiler can turn every case into a sequential integer.
options.explanation: Exhaustive matching is for safety, not integer conversion.

options.text: Because Swift switch statements do not allow a default branch.
options.explanation: Swift switch statements allow a default branch when needed.

options.text: Because Swift requires every enum case to fall through to the next.
options.explanation: Swift switch cases do not fall through by default.

options.text: To make sure your code handles every case so no missed state causes a bug.
options.explanation: Right. Exhaustive matching catches missed cases at compile time.

questions.prompt: What is an associated value in a Swift enumeration?

options.text: Custom data attached to an enum case when you create an instance.
options.explanation: Right. Associated values let cases store custom data that varies per instance.

options.text: A fixed integer assigned by the compiler to every case in the enum.
options.explanation: Fixed constants shared by cases are raw values, not associated values.

options.text: A default value that stays the same for every instance of that case.
options.explanation: Raw values stay the same for every instance of a case; associated values can vary.

options.text: A required raw string name that Swift creates for debugging.
options.explanation: Associated values are custom runtime data, not debug names.

questions.prompt: What is a raw value in a Swift enumeration?

options.text: Custom data that changes each time you create an enum instance.
options.explanation: Custom data per instance is an associated value, not a raw value.

options.text: A fixed constant of one shared type assigned to each case in the enum.
options.explanation: Right. Raw values give every case a fixed constant of the same type.

options.text: A mutable variable that changes when a mutating method runs.
options.explanation: Raw values are fixed constants, not mutable variables.

options.text: A temporary string that Swift creates only during a switch check.
options.explanation: Raw values are part of the enum definition, not temporary switch values.

questions.prompt: What is an enumeration in Swift, and how does it differ from enums in C or Objective-C? Mention whether it is a value or reference type. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Defines a Swift enumeration as a type that holds a fixed group of related choices
Explains that Swift enums do not give integer values to cases by default
States that Swift enums are value types

questions.modelAnswer: In Swift, an enumeration defines a custom type for a fixed group of related choices. Unlike enums in C or Objective-C, Swift enum cases do not get integer numbers by default. Each case is its own distinct value. Swift enums are also value types, so they are copied when assigned or passed to functions.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between raw values and associated values in Swift enums. Can an enum use both? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that raw values are fixed constants of one shared type for all cases
Explains that associated values store custom runtime data per instance
States that an enum cannot use both raw values and associated values together

questions.modelAnswer: Raw values are fixed compile-time constants of one shared type, like Int or String, for every case in an enum. Associated values attach custom runtime data that can differ each time you create a case instance. An enum cannot use both features together. If an enum declares a raw type, its cases cannot have associated values.

questions.prompt: Why does the raw value initializer init?(rawValue:) return an Optional in Swift? What must you do when using it? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that init?(rawValue:) is a failable initializer that returns an Optional
States that it returns nil when the raw value does not match any case
Mentions that you must safely unwrap the optional value (such as with if let or guard let)

questions.modelAnswer: The raw value initializer init?(rawValue:) is a failable initializer that returns an optional enum value. It returns nil when the input raw value does not match any valid case in the enum. Because it might return nil, you must safely unwrap the result using if let or guard let before using it.

questions.prompt: Can Swift enums have properties and methods? What kind of properties are forbidden, and what should you use instead for per-instance data? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that enums can have instance methods, mutating methods, and computed properties
States that enums cannot have stored properties
Mentions that per-instance data must be stored as associated values instead

questions.modelAnswer: Swift enums can have computed properties, instance methods, and mutating methods. However, enums cannot have stored properties. The compiler stops with an error if you declare a stored variable inside an enum. To store custom data per instance, use associated values instead.

questions.prompt: Why does Swift require switch statements on enums to be exhaustive? How does this protect code when new cases are added? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that exhaustive matching ensures every enum case is handled
States that adding a new case causes a compile error in any switch without a default branch
Notes that this compiler check prevents missed cases and runtime bugs

questions.modelAnswer: Swift requires switch statements on enums to be exhaustive so every possible case is handled. When you add a new case, the compiler shows an error at every switch without a default branch. This check forces you to update your code right away, which prevents missed cases and runtime bugs.
